chunks: Muhammad ibn 'Ali ibn Mahbub narrated from Musa ibn 'Umayr, from al-Hasan ibn 'Ali ibn Faddal, from Ibn Bukayr and Tha'labah ibn Maymun, from Burayd, from Abi Ja'far عليه السلام, who said:
From the forehead to the nose—whichever part of that you place upon the ground in sajdah, it suffices for you; but performing sajdah upon all of it is more virtuous.

key_terms.أَجْزَأَكَ: it is sufficient for you; it fulfills the required validity
key_terms.أَفْضَلُ: more virtuous; indicating a preferable manner beyond bare sufficiency
key_terms.الْأَنْفِ: the nose; included here as part of the area extending from the forehead
key_terms.الْجَبْهَةُ: the forehead; the primary area discussed for contact in sajdah

ai.seo_question: What part of the face must touch the ground in sajdah for it to be valid?
ai.summary: This hadith states a legal ruling regarding the area of the face used in sajdah. It teaches that placing any part from the forehead to the nose on the ground is sufficient, while placing the whole of it is more virtuous and preferable.
